reports.committee: Energy Security and Net Zero Committee
reports.title: UK climate leadership at a crossroad
about: Climate change is a global problem that requires a global response. The world is now experiencing the increasingly severe impacts of a rapidly heating climate with intense wildfires, severe droughts, and heavy rainfall leading to destructive floods more frequently and over a wider range.
reports.role: The Energy Security and Net Zero Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and its public bodies, including Ofgem and the Committee on Climate change.

reports.title: The Crown Estate and associated properties: governance and management
about: The Crown Estate is independent of both the government and the Monarch, and has a statutory duty to maintain and enhance the value of the estate and the returns obtained from it.The Royal Household is the body which supports the Sovereign and members of the Royal Family in their official duties, and maintains the occupied royal palaces.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: Critical minerals
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.

reports.title: Fire Safety in Prisons
reports.role: The Justice and Home Affairs Committee was appointed to consider justice and home affairs, including the domestic criminal justice system, and international cooperation in respect of criminal justice, civil justice, migration and asylum.

reports.title: Courts and Tribunals Bill
reports.role: The Constitution Committee examines all public bills for constitutional implications and investigates broad constitutional issues.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: Reforming the water sector: protecting the environment and consumers
about: UK water bodies are affected by a number of high-profile threats including agricultural and sewage pollution. The water sector faces other important concerns such as weak resilience of water supply systems and future water security.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the threats facing UK water, such as rivers and lakes, including pollution from farming and sewage. It also looked at wider worries, such as whether water supplies can cope with problems and whether there will be enough water in future.

reports.title: Scrutiny of International Agreements: UK re-accession to the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)
reports.role: The Committee scrutinises all treaties subject to ratification that are laid before Parliament under the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010 and considers other issues relating to the negotiation, conclusion and implementation of international agreements.

reports.title: Restoration and Renewal of Parliament: Costing and governance
about: More than a million people, including 100,000 school children, pass through the doors of the Palace of Westminster each year. It is a world heritage site, home to one of the busiest parliaments, and considered to be one of the finest examples of 19th-century neo-gothic Victorian architecture in the world.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the cost and running of the work to restore and renew the Palace of Westminster. More than a million people visit it each year, and it is a world heritage site known for its Victorian neo-gothic design.

reports.title: The science and regulation of hair and beauty products and treatments
about: Hair and beauty products (chemicals applied to the hair or body for cosmetic purposes) and treatments (cosmetic procedures typically performed by specialists) can cause harm to consumers if they contain unregulated ingredients or if they are improperly administered.
reports.role: The Science and Technology Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of the Government Office for Science and associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how hair and beauty products and treatments are made safe and regulated. Products can harm people if they contain ingredients that are not regulated, and treatments can harm people if they are not carried out properly.

reports.committee: Energy Security and Net Zero Committee
reports.title: Planning for fusion
reports.inquiry: National Planning Policy Statement on Nuclear Fusion
about: Nuclear fusion is the process that powers the Sun, and for decades humans have been working towards harnessing its remarkable, "clean" power. Now the UK Government has determined that the technology has advanced sufficiently to warrant introducing planning legislation that will facilitate the development of prototypes and demonstrator facilities.
reports.role: The Energy Security and Net Zero Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and its public bodies, including Ofgem and the Committee on Climate change.
reports.plain: The committee looked at planning rules for nuclear fusion, the process that powers the Sun. The Government has decided the technology has advanced enough to bring in planning law that would help prototypes and demonstration sites get built.

reports.title: Report - Making it Count: Numeracy for Life
reports.role: The Numeracy for Life Committee was appointed to consider numeracy in England.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: China and the UK economy: the case for risk-managed growth
about: In this inquiry, the Business and Trade Committee will scrutinise the Government’s approach to economic engagement with China. In particular, it assessed the potential net benefits to the UK of deeper economic integration with China, and how these benefits compare to the risks that closer ties with China may bring.
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the Government deals with China on trade and the economy. It weighed the possible gains for the UK from closer economic ties against the risks that closer ties could bring.

reports.title: The obesity moonshot: making obesity a political priority
about: The committee looked into food and weight management, including treatments for obesity. In 2022, 64% of adults in England were either overweight or living with obesity.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at food and weight management in England, including treatments for obesity. In 2022, 64% of adults in England were overweight or living with obesity.

reports.title: The financial sustainability of the British Council
reports.inquiry: Financial sustainability of the British Council
about: The British Council is an executive non-departmental public body sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). Founded 90 years ago, the Council has a well-established history in promoting UK culture, education and the English language across the globe.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the money position of the British Council, which promotes UK culture, education and the English language around the world. It is a public body backed by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and was founded 90 years ago.

reports.title: Sizewell C
about: Sizewell C is a planned large-scale nuclear power station on the Suffolk coast. Funded by the government in partnership with the energy provider EDF, as well as private finance, the project is projected to cost £40.5bn to £47.7bn.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at Sizewell C, a planned large nuclear power station on the Suffolk coast. The government is paying for it with the energy company EDF and private finance, and it is expected to cost between £40.5bn and £47.7bn.

reports.committee: Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee
reports.title: The Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman's investigations into the Charity Commission
about: This inquiry examined two reports laid by the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman in September 2025 which relate to separate investigations into two complaints about the Charity Commission for England and Wales (the Charity Commission).
reports.role: The Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee (PACAC) is appointed by the House of Commons to examine: constitutional issues; the quality and standards of administration provided by Civil Service departments; and the reports of the Public Service Ombudsman (PSO).
reports.plain: The committee looked at two reports the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman laid in September 2025. Each came from an investigation into a complaint about the Charity Commission for England and Wales.

reports.title: Home and travel insurance regulation: more for the FCA to do
reports.inquiry: Regulation of the consumer insurance market
reports.role: The Financial Services Regulation Committee was appointed to consider the regulation of financial services.

reports.title: Food and Weight Management: Modernising obesity treatment
about: The committee looked into food and weight management, including treatments for obesity. In 2022, 64% of adults in England were either overweight or living with obesity.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at food and weight management in England, including treatments for obesity. In 2022, 64% of adults in England were overweight or living with obesity.

reports.title: Defence in the High North
about: The inquiry examined the current and emerging threats in the region. It will ask what the UK’s defence and security interests are, and whether we have the correct strategies, capabilities and alliances to counter these threats, particularly from Russia.
reports.role: The Defence Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration, and policy of the Ministry of Defence and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the threats in the High North, the Arctic region, now and in future. It asked what the UK's defence and security interests are there, and whether the UK has the right plans, equipment and allies to deal with them, especially threats from Russia.

reports.committee: Energy Security and Net Zero Committee
reports.title: The cost of energy
about: In October last year the Committee published its interim report on the high costs of energy in the UK making recommendations on how costs fall on consumers in the retail side of the sector.
reports.role: The Energy Security and Net Zero Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and its public bodies, including Ofgem and the Committee on Climate change.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: A burning issue: managing wildfire risk
about: The UK is facing increasingly frequent and severe environmental and weather-related events, including storms, flooding, heatwaves and wildfires. These, and other weather and climate related events, pose growing risks to public health, infrastructure, food production, and the natural environment.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at wildfires and how to manage the risk. The UK is facing more frequent and more severe storms, floods, heatwaves and wildfires, which put public health, infrastructure, food production and nature at growing risk.

reports.title: UK Research and Innovation: Investment in research infrastructure
about: Government has an ambition for the UK to be “one of the top three places in the world to create, invest in and scale-up a fast-growing technology business by 2035”. Overseen by the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) will be central to achieving this aim.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how UK Research and Innovation spends money on research buildings and equipment. The Government wants the UK to be one of the top three places in the world to start and grow a technology business by 2035, and this body is central to that aim.

reports.title: Fixed link connectivity in Scotland’s islands
about: Transport infrastructure plays an important role among island communities, supporting local economies and ensuring access to essential services. In Scotland, geographic barriers and limited transport options can restrict mobility and contribute to depopulation.
reports.role: The Scottish Affairs Committee scrutinises the expenditure, administration and policies of the Scotland Office, and its associated bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at fixed links, such as bridges or tunnels, to Scotland's islands. Transport matters to island communities because it supports local businesses and access to essential services, while poor links can limit travel and contribute to people leaving.

reports.title: New Towns: Commit and Build
reports.role: The Built Environment Committee was appointed to consider matters relating to the built environment, including policies relating to housing, planning, transport and infrastructure.

reports.title: Representation of the People Bill
reports.role: The Constitution Committee examines all public bills for constitutional implications and investigates broad constitutional issues.

reports.title: Scrutiny of International Agreements: Agreement in respect of Gibraltar between the European Union and the European Atomic Energy Community, of the one part, and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, of the other part
about: The report Scrutiny of International Agreements: Agreement in respect of Gibraltar between the European Union and the European Atomic Energy Community, of the one part, and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, of the other part was published 14 October 2026 and debated in Grand Committee on 20 October 2026
reports.plain: The committee published a report on the agreement about Gibraltar between the European Union and the UK. It was published on 14 October 2026 and debated in Grand Committee on 20 October 2026.

reports.title: Annual Report of the Chair of the Committee of Public Accounts (2026)
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.

reports.committee: Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee
reports.title: BBC Royal Charter Review
about: The Culture, Media and Sport Committee looked at the future of the BBC as part of a new inquiry into the Royal Charter Review. The review of the BBC Charter, which sets out how the broadcaster is governed, regulated and funded, takes place about every ten years.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the future of the BBC as part of the review of its Royal Charter. The Charter sets out how the BBC is run, regulated and paid for, and it is reviewed about every ten years.

reports.title: The Office for Budget Responsibility: Time for change?
about: The Treasury Committee examined the Office for Budget Responsibility's (OBR) current effectiveness and record, and explore whether and how it might need to change.
reports.role: The Treasury Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of HM Treasury, HM Revenue & Customs, and associated public bodies, including the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how well the Office for Budget Responsibility works and what its record has been. It also asked whether the body should change, and if so how.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: The future of Thames Water and special administration
about: UK water bodies are affected by a number of high-profile threats including agricultural and sewage pollution. The water sector faces other important concerns such as weak resilience of water supply systems and future water security.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the threats facing UK water, including pollution from farming and sewage. It also looked at wider worries, such as whether water supplies can cope with problems and whether there will be enough water in future.

reports.title: Government's intervention in British Steel Ltd
about: Rising energy prices, decarbonisation, uncertainty over trade and tariffs from the EU and US, as well as increased global competition have placed the UK’s steel industry under significant pressure in recent years. In January 2026, British Steel employed 4,052 permanent staff and had a production capacity of three million tonnes per year.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Government's step in to keep British Steel going. The UK steel industry has been under pressure from rising energy prices, the move to cleaner production, trade uncertainty and global competition. In January 2026 the company employed 4,052 permanent staff.

reports.committee: Energy Security and Net Zero Committee
reports.title: Zero sum game: How the UK can reframe the energy transition
reports.inquiry: Building support for the energy transition
about: The ability of the Government to make difficult decisions and to change the way in which energy is generated and used in the UK will depend on being able to bring people along with it. A vocal opposition to ‘net zero’ - including the energy transition - has grown in strength, political consensus has fractured and with it potentially the will to carry it through.
reports.role: The Energy Security and Net Zero Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and its public bodies, including Ofgem and the Committee on Climate change.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the UK can change the way it makes and uses energy. It asked how the Government can bring people along, as vocal opposition to net zero has grown and political agreement on it has broken down.

reports.title: UK International Climate Finance: Sustaining Commitments and Impact Amid a Shrinking Aid Budget
about: UK ICF was launched in 2011 as Official Development Assistance (ODA). It plays a crucial role in fulfilling the UK’s obligations under the Paris Climate Agreement and advancing the Government’s wider ambition to establish the UK as a global leader in international climate action.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at UK International Climate Finance, money the UK gives to help other countries deal with climate change. It started in 2011 and helps the UK meet its duties under the Paris Climate Agreement.

reports.title: Large Print - 2nd Report - UK International Climate Finance: Sustaining Commitments and Impact Amid a Shrinking Aid Budget
about: UK ICF was launched in 2011 as Official Development Assistance (ODA). It plays a crucial role in fulfilling the UK’s obligations under the Paris Climate Agreement and advancing the Government’s wider ambition to establish the UK as a global leader in international climate action.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at UK International Climate Finance, money the UK gives to help other countries deal with climate change. It started in 2011 and helps the UK meet its duties under the Paris Climate Agreement. This is the large print version of the report.

reports.title: Gambling Harm-Time for Action: Follow-up report
reports.inquiry: Social and Economic Impact of the Gambling Industry - follow-up
about: In May 2025 the Liaison Committee wrote to the Minister for Museums, Heritage and Gambling at the Department for Culture, Media and Sport undertaking initial follow-up.

reports.title: Securing Scotland's future: Defence skills and jobs
reports.inquiry: Securing Scotland’s Future: Defence Skills and Jobs
about: The UK Government has committed to increase defence spending to 2.6% of GDP by 2027, with plans to reach 3% in the next Parliament. Given Scotland’s significant role in the UK’s defence sector, this inquiry explored how Scotland’s economy and job market can benefit, particularly through the creation of highly skilled jobs.
reports.role: The Scottish Affairs Committee scrutinises the expenditure, administration and policies of the Scotland Office, and its associated bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how Scotland's economy and workers can gain from more UK defence spending. The Government has committed to raise defence spending to 2.6% of national income by 2027, and the inquiry focused on creating highly skilled jobs.

reports.title: Human Rights and the Regulation of AI
about: The inquiry explored what regulation might be required in order to safeguard human rights when AI technologies are being developed and used, and any implications this might have for future legislation. Many argue that AI technologies can offer great benefits to individuals and society – for example, assisting in decision-making and improving productivity.
reports.role: The Joint Committee on Human Rights consists of twelve members, appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords, to examine matters relating to human rights within the United Kingdom, as well as scrutinising every Government Bill for its compatibility with human rights.
reports.plain: The committee looked at what rules might be needed to protect human rights as AI is developed and used, and what that might mean for future laws. Many people argue AI can bring benefits, such as helping with decisions and making work more productive.

reports.title: Appointment of the Chair of the Care Quality Commission
reports.inquiry: Pre-appointment hearing: Chair of the Care Quality Commission
about: Pre-appointment hearing: Chair of the Care Quality Commission
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee held a hearing before the Chair of the Care Quality Commission was appointed. This is known as a pre-appointment hearing.

reports.title: Regulation of water, energy and broadband
about: The Public Accounts Committee’s 2025 report on water sector regulation found that a failing sector had been left to flounder, with piecemeal regulators missing in action, further scrutinising the work of Ofwat in January 2026. Its inquiry into improving broadband in 2021 found that digital inequality was compounding the economic inequality harshly exposed by the COVID pandemic.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how water, energy and broadband are regulated. Its earlier work found that the water regulators had left a failing sector to struggle, and that digital inequality was adding to economic inequality.

reports.committee: Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee
reports.title: The work of the UK Statistics Authority
about: The Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee examined the performance of the UK Statistics Authority (UKSA), and its two executive offices, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) and the Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR).
reports.role: The Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee (PACAC) is appointed by the House of Commons to examine: constitutional issues; the quality and standards of administration provided by Civil Service departments; and the reports of the Public Service Ombudsman (PSO).
reports.plain: The committee looked at how well the UK Statistics Authority is doing its job. That includes its two executive offices, the Office for National Statistics and the Office for Statistics Regulation.

reports.title: Cosmetic procedures: follow-up
reports.inquiry: Health impacts of breast implants and other cosmetic procedures
about: The Women and Equalities Committee examined the health impacts of breast implants and other cosmetic procedures. This inquiry explored the safety and regulation of both surgical and non-surgical cosmetic procedures, including how risks are communicated and managed.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the health effects of breast implants and other cosmetic procedures. It asked how safe and how well regulated surgical and non-surgical procedures are, including how the risks are explained and managed.

reports.title: Large Print - 2nd Report - Cosmetic procedures: follow-up
reports.inquiry: Health impacts of breast implants and other cosmetic procedures
about: The Women and Equalities Committee examined the health impacts of breast implants and other cosmetic procedures. This inquiry explored the safety and regulation of both surgical and non-surgical cosmetic procedures, including how risks are communicated and managed.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the health effects of breast implants and other cosmetic procedures. It asked how safe and how well regulated surgical and non-surgical procedures are, including how the risks are explained and managed. This is the large print version of the report.

reports.title: Scrutiny of International Agreements: Treaty between the UK and Poland on a Security and Defence Partnership
reports.role: The Committee scrutinises all treaties subject to ratification that are laid before Parliament under the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010 and considers other issues relating to the negotiation, conclusion and implementation of international agreements.

reports.title: Government compensation schemes
about: When public bodies’ failures harm UK citizens, they should expect to be fairly and swiftly compensated. Failings in such schemes were identified in the PAC’s previous reports on the Windrush Compensation Scheme, Equitable Life and the British Steel Pension Scheme.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at government compensation schemes. When public bodies fail and harm people, those people should expect fair and quick compensation, but the committee's earlier reports on the Windrush, Equitable Life and British Steel Pension schemes found failings.

reports.title: Economic growth in Northern Ireland: Final Report
reports.inquiry: Economic growth in Northern Ireland: new and emerging sectors
about: Kickstarting economic growth is the number one mission for this Government’s term in office. In this inquiry, the committee examined plans to deliver economic growth in Northern Ireland, including the recent UK Industrial Strategy, with a particular reference to emerging sectors or ‘industries of the future’.
reports.role: The Committee examines the expenditure, administration and policy of the Northern Ireland Office and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at plans to grow Northern Ireland's economy, including the UK Industrial Strategy. It paid particular attention to new sectors that could become the industries of the future.

reports.title: Legislative Scrutiny: Northern Ireland Troubles Bill
about: The Northern Ireland Troubles Bill was introduced into the House of Commons on 14 October 2025 and is intended to repeal and replace various aspects of the Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy and Reconciliation) Act 2023, as well as to reform and supplement the wider approach of dealing with the legacy of the Troubles. The Joint Committee on Human Rights is scrutinising the Bill’s compatibility with human rights.
reports.role: The Joint Committee on Human Rights consists of twelve members, appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords, to examine matters relating to human rights within the United Kingdom, as well as scrutinising every Government Bill for its compatibility with human rights.
reports.plain: The committee checked the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill against human rights standards. The Bill was introduced in the House of Commons on 14 October 2025 and would repeal and replace parts of an earlier 2023 Act on dealing with the legacy of the Troubles.

reports.title: Human Rights of Children in the Social Care System in England
about: This inquiry considered the extent to which the human rights of children in England are protected in the social care system.
reports.role: The Joint Committee on Human Rights consists of twelve members, appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords, to examine matters relating to human rights within the United Kingdom, as well as scrutinising every Government Bill for its compatibility with human rights.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how well the human rights of children in England are protected when they are in the social care system.

reports.title: Easy Read - 2nd Report - Human Rights of Children in the Social Care System in England
reports.inquiry: Human Rights of Children in the Social Care System in England
about: This inquiry considered the extent to which the human rights of children in England are protected in the social care system.
reports.role: The Joint Committee on Human Rights consists of twelve members, appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords, to examine matters relating to human rights within the United Kingdom, as well as scrutinising every Government Bill for its compatibility with human rights.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how well the human rights of children in England are protected when they are in the social care system. This is the Easy Read version of the report.

reports.title: Paws for concern: pets, parasites and pollution
about: This short inquiry considered pet parasite medication (PPM), with a focus on treatments containing pesticides of concern such as fipronil and imidacloprid. The inquiry sought to understand distribution pathways, and the impact of PPM use and non-use on biodiversity and human health.
reports.role: The Environment and Climate Change Committee was appointed to consider the environment and climate change.
reports.plain: The committee looked at pet parasite medication, such as flea and tick treatments, especially those containing the pesticides fipronil and imidacloprid. It asked how these products reach the environment and what using or not using them means for wildlife and human health.

reports.title: Shifting heaven and earth? The Afghan data breach and resettlement schemes
reports.inquiry: Afghan Data Breach and Resettlement Schemes
about: This inquiry examined the circumstances behind and the consequences of a major data breach in February 2022 from the Ministry of Defence. The breach involved the personal data of thousands of Afghan applicants for resettlement to the UK and their families, potentially putting these people at risk of reprisals.
reports.role: The Defence Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration, and policy of the Ministry of Defence and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at a major data breach by the Ministry of Defence in February 2022. It involved the personal data of thousands of Afghans who had applied to be resettled in the UK, and their families, and could have put them at risk of reprisals.

reports.title: Youth employment, education and training
about: Nearly one million young people aged 16–24 are not in employment, education or training (NEET). This is a worrying statistic given the harm that being NEET can do to young people’s prospects and wellbeing.
reports.role: The Work and Pensions Committee looks into the policies and spending of the Department for Work and Pensions, including benefits for people in and out of work, state pensions and how private pensions are regulated.
reports.plain: The committee looked at young people who are not in work, education or training. Nearly one million people aged 16 to 24 are in this position, which can harm their prospects and wellbeing.

reports.title: Reading for Pleasure
about: Reading brings a range of benefits to children, young people and their families, but the number of children reading for pleasure is declining rapidly. This inquiry looked at the reasons behind this decline and what can be done to reverse this trend.
reports.role: The Education Committee scrutinises the work of the Department for Education, covering children’s social care, schools, colleges, the early years and higher education.
reports.plain: The committee looked at why fewer children are reading for pleasure. Reading brings many benefits to children, young people and their families, and the committee asked what can be done to reverse the decline.

reports.title: Pre-appointment hearing: His Majesty’s Chief Inspector of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Authorities
about: His Majesty’s Chief Inspector of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Authorities is responsible for ensuring the inspection of police forces and fire & rescue authorities, and reporting publicly on their efficiency and effectiveness. The role is subject to pre-appointment scrutiny by the Home Affairs Committee before any appointment by Ministers.
reports.role: The Home Affairs Committee is a cross-party committee of MPs responsible for scrutinising the work of the Home Office and its associated bodies.
reports.plain: The committee held a hearing before the new Chief Inspector of Constabulary and Fire and Rescue Authorities was appointed. This person makes sure police forces and fire and rescue authorities are inspected and reports publicly on how efficient and effective they are.

reports.title: Access to Justice: Legal Aid
about: This inquiry examined how advice and legal services are adapting to secure access to justice across civil, criminal, and family law, and the impacts of the cyber-attack on the Legal Aid Agency. In 2022-23, the Justice Committee undertook a broad inquiry on the Future of Legal Aid, looking at the challenges facing legal aid clients and providers and how they might be tackled.
reports.role: The Justice Committee examines the policies and spending of the Ministry of Justice (and associated public bodies).
reports.plain: The committee looked at how advice and legal services are adapting so people can get access to justice in civil, criminal and family law. It also looked at the effects of the cyber-attack on the Legal Aid Agency.

reports.title: Unlocking land for housing
about: A shortage of land is cited by government as underpinning the housing crisis. The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) supports programmes aimed at boosting land supply for housing development which is deemed necessary to ‘unlock’.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the Government is trying to free up land for building homes. The Government says a shortage of land underlies the housing crisis, and the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government runs programmes to increase the supply.

reports.title: Acting Select Committee Chairs
reports.role: The Modernisation Committee is a cross-party committee of MPs that considers reforms to House of Commons procedures, standards, and working practices.

reports.title: Appointment of Professor Jonathan Haskel as Chair of the Office for Budget Responsibility
reports.role: The Treasury Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of HM Treasury, HM Revenue & Customs, and associated public bodies, including the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority.

reports.title: Food and Weight Management: Fixing the food environment
about: The committee looked into food and weight management, including treatments for obesity. In 2022, 64% of adults in England were either overweight or living with obesity.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at food and weight management in England, including treatments for obesity. In 2022, 64% of adults in England were overweight or living with obesity.

reports.title: Government shared services
about: In order to operate effectively, Government Departments need access to a range of back-office functions such as human resources and payroll. Since 2004, the government has attempted to centralise these functions to cut the cost of services and improve the consistency of data.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how government departments share back-office services such as human resources and payroll. Since 2004, the Government has tried to bring these functions together to cut costs and make data more consistent.

reports.title: Black people’s experiences of homelessness
about: This inquiry examines why and how Black people face disproportionate risks of homelessness. It will also consider what measures the Government should include in its upcoming cross-departmental homelessness and rough sleeping strategy.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee looked at why Black people face a higher risk of homelessness. It also looked at what the Government should include in its coming strategy on homelessness and rough sleeping, which covers several departments.

reports.title: Large Print: 1st Report - Black people’s experiences of homelessness
about: This inquiry examines why and how Black people face disproportionate risks of homelessness. It will also consider what measures the Government should include in its upcoming cross-departmental homelessness and rough sleeping strategy.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee looked at why Black people face a higher risk of homelessness. It also looked at what the Government should include in its coming strategy on homelessness and rough sleeping. This is the large print version of the report.

reports.title: The UK’s development partnership with Nigeria
about: Nigeria was the sixth largest recipient of UK Official Development Assistance in 2023 with over £100m allocated. This was a reduction from third place in 2022 when it received £110m.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the UK's development partnership with Nigeria. In 2023 Nigeria was the sixth largest recipient of UK aid, with over £100m, down from third place in 2022 when it received £110m.

reports.title: Financial Inclusion Strategy
about: The Treasury Committee examined the Government's recently published Financial Inclusion Strategy, which sets out plans to improve access to financial products and services across of the UK.
reports.role: The Treasury Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of HM Treasury, HM Revenue & Customs, and associated public bodies, including the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Government's new Financial Inclusion Strategy. It sets out plans to make it easier for people across the UK to get financial products and services.

reports.committee: Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee
reports.title: Protecting built heritage
about: The Culture, Media and Sport Committee examined the importance of built heritage in the UK and the barriers to its preservation. The inquiry examined issues with funding and whether current finance models are suitable and accessible.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at why historic buildings and places matter in the UK and what stops them being preserved. It asked about funding, and whether the current ways of paying for this are suitable and easy to use.

reports.title: Transition to State Pension Age
about: The last time the State Pension age went up there was a jump in the number of pre-pensioners (people aged 60+ but below pension age) in poverty. This group are the joint poorest among working age adults.
reports.role: The Work and Pensions Committee looks into the policies and spending of the Department for Work and Pensions, including benefits for people in and out of work, state pensions and how private pensions are regulated.
reports.plain: The committee looked at people approaching State Pension age. When the age last went up, more people aged 60 or over but below pension age fell into poverty, and this group is among the poorest of working-age adults.

reports.title: Large business tax compliance
about: Taxes from the nation’s large businesses account for around 40% of the total tax revenue collected by HM Revenue & Customs, while representing less than 0.1% of UK business. HMRC’s large business directorate works with approximately 2,000 of these businesses (typically those with an annual turnover of more than £200m) to make sure they pay the right tax.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at whether large businesses pay the right tax. They bring in around 40% of the tax HM Revenue and Customs collects, though they are less than 0.1% of UK businesses. HMRC works with about 2,000 of them, typically those with turnover above £200m.

reports.title: The appointment of Peter Mandelson as British Ambassador to the United States
reports.inquiry: Work of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
about: The Committee periodically questions the Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs and the Permanent Under-Secretary, alongside other relevant officials on the overall management of the FCDO, topical or urgent matters and the Committee’s inquiry work.
reports.role: The Foreign Affairs Committee examines the expenditure, administration and policy of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and other bodies associated with the Foreign Office and within the Committee's remit, including the British Council.

reports.title: Science diplomacy: Sovereignty, strategy, and the global race
about: The committee looked into the role of science diplomacy and research and development (R&D) in supporting the UK Government’s growth missions, enhancing the UK’s international influence, and contributing to national security.
reports.role: The Science and Technology Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of the Government Office for Science and associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how science and research can help the UK abroad. It asked how they support the Government's growth missions, increase the UK's international influence and help national security.

reports.title: Student loans: Broken and unfair?
reports.inquiry: Student loans and taxation of graduates
about: In 1998 the Government first introduced tuition fees for higher education. Since then, the costs borne by students for their tuition has risen, and correspondingly so has the amount that students can borrow through student loans.
reports.role: The Treasury Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of HM Treasury, HM Revenue & Customs, and associated public bodies, including the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority.
reports.plain: The committee looked at student loans. Tuition fees for higher education were first brought in by the Government in 1998. Since then the cost to students has risen, and so has the amount they can borrow through student loans.

reports.title: Business events
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: The UK-US economic relationship: 250 years on
about: The Business and Trade Committee is conducting its bi-annual stock take on the UK-US economic and trade agreements, building on its baseline report US Economic Prosperity Deal (HC 1306, 2024–26). Since that report, the Economic Prosperity Deal (EPD) framework has been extended through a Technology Prosperity Deal (TPD) and an agreement on pharmaceutical tariffs.
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee carried out its twice-yearly check on the UK-US trade and economic agreements. Since its last report, the Economic Prosperity Deal has been extended through a Technology Prosperity Deal and an agreement on pharmaceutical tariffs.

reports.title: Independent Commission on Adult Social Care
about: The Independent Commission on Adult Social Care, led by Baroness Louise Casey, was launched on 29 April 2025. The Commission is expected make clear recommendations to define and build the adult social care system that will meet the current and future needs of the population.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Independent Commission on Adult Social Care, led by Baroness Louise Casey, which was launched on 29 April 2025. The Commission is expected to make clear recommendations for an adult social care system that meets current and future needs.

reports.committee: Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee
reports.title: Housing Conditions in the Private Rented Sector
about: The committee looked into the condition of homes in England.
reports.role: The Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee scrutinises the policy, administration and spending of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the condition of homes in England, in the private rented sector.

reports.title: Northern Powerhouse Rail
about: Since 2014, successive governments have acknowledged the limitations of rail infrastructure in the North of England. Several large cities - including Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester, Newcastle and Sheffield - are poorly served by transport connections.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at Northern Powerhouse Rail. Since 2014, successive governments have accepted that rail in the North of England is limited, and several large cities, including Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester, Newcastle and Sheffield, are poorly served by transport links.

reports.role: The Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee (PACAC) is appointed by the House of Commons to examine: constitutional issues; the quality and standards of administration provided by Civil Service departments; and the reports of the Public Service Ombudsman (PSO).

reports.title: Financial resilience of government-sponsored museums and galleries
about: Fifteen national museums and galleries, including the British Museum and the Science Museum, are sponsored by the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), with free access afforded to their permanent collections as a result.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how financially secure government-sponsored museums and galleries are. Fifteen national museums and galleries, including the British Museum and the Science Museum, are sponsored by the Department for Culture, Media and Sport, and free access to their permanent collections is provided as a result.

reports.title: Settlement, Citizenship and Integration
reports.role: The Justice and Home Affairs Committee was appointed to consider justice and home affairs, including the domestic criminal justice system, and international cooperation in respect of criminal justice, civil justice, migration and asylum.

reports.title: Employment support for disabled people: Connect to Work
about: With the disability employment gap persistently at nearly 30%, the Government has announced it will spend an additional £2.2 billion on employment support over the next four years. The Committee is exploring the reasons behind the disability employment gap, scrutinising government programmes to support disabled people into work and making recommendations for future support.
reports.role: The Work and Pensions Committee looks into the policies and spending of the Department for Work and Pensions, including benefits for people in and out of work, state pensions and how private pensions are regulated.
reports.plain: The committee looked at why disabled people are less likely to be in work, a gap that has stayed at nearly 30%. The Government plans to spend an extra £2.2 billion on employment support over the next four years, and the committee scrutinised those programmes.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: UK-EU relations a decade on
about: At a Joint Summit in May 2025, the UK and EU agreed to a Security and Defence Partnership, and published a “Common Understanding”, setting out shared commitments to deepen cooperation. Progress since that initial summit has been limited, with core areas for agreement still to conclude.
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at UK-EU relations. At a Joint Summit in May 2025 the UK and EU agreed a Security and Defence Partnership. Progress since then has been limited, with core areas for agreement still to be concluded.

reports.title: Draft Human Rights Act 1998 (Remedial) Order: Judicial Immunity: Second Report
reports.inquiry: Proposal for a draft Human Rights Act 1998 (Remedial) Order 2025
about: Background  Section 9(3) of the Human Rights Act 1998 provides that in proceedings under that Act in respect of a judicial act done in good faith, damages may not be awarded except in two circumstances. The first is to compensate a person to the extent required by Article 5(5) of the European Convention on Human Rights (‘ECHR’) (deprivation of liberty).
reports.role: The Joint Committee on Human Rights consists of twelve members, appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords, to examine matters relating to human rights within the United Kingdom, as well as scrutinising every Government Bill for its compatibility with human rights.
reports.plain: The committee looked at a draft order to change the Human Rights Act 1998 on judicial immunity. The Act says that when a judge acts in good faith, damages can be awarded only in two circumstances. The first is to compensate someone for being deprived of their liberty.

reports.committee: Energy Security and Net Zero Committee
reports.title: Get connected: How community energy can turbocharge the transition
about: The committee looked into community energy.
reports.role: The Energy Security and Net Zero Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and its public bodies, including Ofgem and the Committee on Climate change.
reports.plain: The committee looked at community energy and how it could help speed up the move to cleaner energy.

reports.committee: Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee
reports.title: Cultural touring in the EU
reports.inquiry: State of Play: Performing arts touring in the EU
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee.

reports.title: Health Bill 2026-27
about: The bill was introduced its Health Bill the House of Commons on 14 May 2026. The main purpose of the bill would be to abolish NHSE and transfer its functions to either ICBs or the Department of Health and Social Care, including transferring some powers directly to the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Health Bill, which was introduced in the House of Commons on 14 May 2026. Its main purpose would be to abolish NHS England and move its functions to other bodies or to the Department of Health and Social Care, including some powers going directly to the Secretary of State.

reports.title: The Access to Work scheme
about: The Department for Work & Pensions (DWP) funds and administers the Access to Work scheme. Introduced in 1994, it is designed to help disabled people and those with health conditions.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Access to Work scheme. The Department for Work and Pensions pays for and runs it, and it has helped disabled people and those with health conditions since it began in 1994.

reports.title: Courts and Tribunals Bill
reports.inquiry: Legislative scrutiny: Courts and Tribunals Bill
about: The Bill was introduced in the House of Commons on 25 February 2026 and is due to have its Second Reading debate on 10 March. Dates for Committee stage are yet to be confirmed.
reports.role: The Justice Committee examines the policies and spending of the Ministry of Justice (and associated public bodies).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which was introduced in the House of Commons on 25 February 2026. Its Second Reading debate was due on 10 March, and dates for the next stage were yet to be confirmed.

reports.title: Regulating for growth
about: When regulation is carried out well, it can be essential for the promotion of economic growth and investment. Poorly-instituted regulation can depress investment and inhibit growth.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how regulation affects growth. Done well, regulation can be essential for promoting growth and investment. Done badly, it can hold investment back and stop growth.

reports.title: Raising the standard: licensing of taxis and private hire vehicles
reports.inquiry: Licensing of taxis and private hire vehicles
about: Taxis and private hire vehicles (PHVs) form a key part of the transport network, particularly for people who face barriers to using other forms of transport and as a driver of the nighttime economy. However, the current system for regulating these vehicles can vary across different licensing authorities, creating inconsistencies and raising questions about how effective present standards are.
reports.role: The Transport Committee is nominated by the House of Commons to scrutinise the Department for Transport.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how taxis and private hire vehicles are licensed. They are a key part of the transport network, but the rules can vary between licensing authorities, which creates inconsistencies and raises questions about how effective the standards are.

reports.committee: Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee
reports.title: Affordability of Home Ownership
about: The committee looked into the affordability of home ownership. Its focus is on people who are looking to buy property for themselves and their families to live in (owner-occupier), as opposed to those who purchase property to rent out as private accommodation (buy-to-let) or as speculative investment.
reports.role: The Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee scrutinises the policy, administration and spending of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how affordable it is to buy a home. It focused on people buying a home for themselves and their families to live in, rather than on people buying to rent out or as an investment.

reports.title: Jagged Justice: Prisons, Probation and Rehabilitation in Wales
reports.inquiry: Prisons, Probation and Rehabilitation in Wales
about: Criminal justice in Wales exists within a unique policy environment, with prisons, probation and rehabilitation reserved to the UK Government, and key intersecting services like health, education and housing devolved to the Welsh Government. Wales is also unique in that, despite having five adult male prison facilities and a young offender institution, it has no prison for adult women.
reports.role: The Welsh Affairs Committee is responsible for scrutinising the expenditure, administration and policies of the Wales Office, and the policies of the UK Government as a whole that have an impact in Wales.
reports.plain: The committee looked at prisons, probation and rehabilitation in Wales. These are the responsibility of the UK Government, while health, education and housing are devolved to the Welsh Government. Wales has five adult male prisons and a young offender institution, but no prison for adult women.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: Investing in the UK economy
about: The Government has made economic growth its “number one mission”, aiming to secure the highest sustained growth in the G7. Yet the UK has consistently lagged behind its peers and in 2025, the IMF projected UK growth at just 1.2%—below most major competitors.
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how to boost investment in the UK economy. The Government has made economic growth its number one mission, but the UK has lagged behind its peers, and in 2025 the IMF projected UK growth of just 1.2%.

reports.title: MoD follow-up Spring 2026
reports.inquiry: Ministry of Defence Annual Report and Accounts 2024-25
about: In November 2025, the National Audit Office’s Comptroller & Auditor General (C&AG) published his qualified opinion on the Ministry of Defence’s (MOD) Accounts 2024-25. This identified a value of £1.5bn in legacy projects carried out by the Atomic Weapons Establishment, which helps deliver the UK’s nuclear deterrent, the value of which had remained unchanged for several years.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee followed up on the Ministry of Defence's accounts. In November 2025 the National Audit Office gave a qualified opinion on the 2024-25 accounts, which found £1.5bn of legacy projects at the Atomic Weapons Establishment whose value had stayed the same for several years.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: A sustainable veterinary workforce
about: Animal and plant diseases and pests have far-reaching impacts on the environment, agricultural and horticultural sectors, trade, human health, animal welfare, and the food that we eat.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the future of the veterinary workforce. Animal and plant diseases and pests have wide effects on the environment, farming, trade, human health, animal welfare and the food we eat.

reports.title: An analysis of the asylum system
about: In December 2024, government committed to “restore order to the asylum and immigration system,” with a number of interventions and changes to policy including the UK-France treaty targeting illegal crossings and the pilot ‘one in, one out’ scheme enabling returns of failed asylum seekers.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the asylum system. In December 2024 the Government committed to restore order to it, with changes that included the UK-France treaty on illegal crossings and a pilot one in, one out scheme for returning failed asylum seekers.

reports.title: Stablecoins: waiting for regulation
reports.inquiry: Growth and proposed regulation of stablecoins in the UK
about: This inquiry examined the development of, and proposed regulatory response to, stablecoins in the UK. In particular, the inquiry examined the extent to which stablecoins might disrupt the traditional models of provision of financial services, including for banking and payments services.
reports.role: The Financial Services Regulation Committee was appointed to consider the regulation of financial services.
reports.plain: The committee looked at stablecoins, a type of digital currency, and how they might be regulated in the UK. It asked whether they could disrupt traditional banking and payments services.

reports.title: Supporting people with frailty outside hospitals
about: More than one in ten people over the age of 65 and up to half the population aged over 85 live with frailty. NHS England describes a person living with frailty, which has a strong link with ageing, as being at high risk of falls, immobility, delirium, incontinence, side effects of medication, admission to hospital or the need for long-term care.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at support for people with frailty outside hospitals. More than one in ten people over 65 and up to half of those over 85 live with frailty, which is strongly linked to ageing and raises the risk of falls and of needing hospital or long-term care.

reports.title: Rewiring the state: Delivering digital government
about: Following the general election, the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) announced plans to become the “digital centre of government”.
reports.role: The Science and Technology Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of the Government Office for Science and associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the Government is moving to digital services. After the general election, the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology announced plans to become the digital centre of government.

reports.title: The MoD’s tackling of economic crime and misconduct
about: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) responds to economic threats and investigates fraud and corruption perpetrated against it through several police forces, including its Fraud Defence team, MoD Police, and the Service police forces, as well as through its own central team. MoD’s last public estimate of its exposure to fraud risk was £1.3bn in 2021-22.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the Ministry of Defence tackles economic crime and misconduct. It investigates fraud and corruption against it through several police forces and its own central team. Its last public estimate of its exposure to fraud risk was £1.3bn in 2021-22.

reports.committee: Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee
reports.title: Pre-legislative scrutiny of the draft Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill
about: On 27 January 2026, the Government published a draft Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill for pre-legislative scrutiny. The Government has asked the HCLG Committee to investigate whether the proposed reforms in the draft Bill will be effective, and what changes the Government could make to improve the draft Bill before the final version is introduced to Parliament.
reports.role: The Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee scrutinises the policy, administration and spending of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the draft Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill, which the Government published on 27 January 2026. The Government asked it to check whether the proposed reforms would work and what changes could improve the draft before the final version goes to Parliament.

reports.title: Policing and security in Northern Ireland
about: 2026 marks 25 years since the establishment of the PSNI following the recommendations of the Patten review on policing. This inquiry examined how far the objectives and aspirations of the Patten review have been realised, and explore the key challenges facing policing and security in Northern Ireland today—particularly in areas that remain under UK Government co-ordination and funding.
reports.role: The Committee examines the expenditure, administration and policy of the Northern Ireland Office and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at policing and security in Northern Ireland. 2026 marks 25 years since the PSNI was set up following the Patten review, and the inquiry asked how far the review's aims have been met and what challenges remain today.

reports.title: Promoting Wales for Inward Investment
about: Inward investment, a term often used interchangeably with Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), refers to cross-border investment from one country to another and which aims to establish a lasting interest and effective voice in an enterprise. In FDI statistics, an effective voice means owning 10% or more of the equity share capital in an enterprise.
reports.role: The Welsh Affairs Committee is responsible for scrutinising the expenditure, administration and policies of the Wales Office, and the policies of the UK Government as a whole that have an impact in Wales.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how to attract inward investment to Wales. This means investment from one country in another that gives the investor a lasting interest in a business, usually by owning 10% or more of its shares.

reports.title: Competition and market functioning in the UK live music industry
about: The Business and Trade Committee is exploring issues impacting competition and market functioning within the UK’s live music industry, including the role of the CMA in regulation of the sector.
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at competition and how well the market works in the UK live music industry. That included the part played by the CMA, the competition regulator, in overseeing the sector.

reports.title: Healthy Ageing: physical activity in an ageing society
about: The committee looked into the role of physical activity in improving the health and wellbeing of our older population. Progress on improving healthy life expectancy in England has stalled and people are spending longer living with ill health in their older years.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how physical activity can improve the health and wellbeing of older people. Progress on healthy life expectancy in England has stalled, and people are spending longer living with ill health in their older years.

reports.title: NAO financial audit insights 2024-25
about: The National Audit Office (NAO) performs financial audits of over 400 public organisations, overseeing £1.2trillion in spending, providing assurance to Parliament as it does on how taxpayers’ money is being spent. It establishes whether organisations’ financial statements are true and fair, and whether what is being spent and collected is in accordance with Parliament’s intentions.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the National Audit Office's financial audits. It audits over 400 public organisations that oversee £1.2 trillion of spending, and checks that their accounts are true and fair and that money is spent and collected as Parliament intended.

reports.title: Growing up in the online world: The Education Committee’s response to the Government’s consultation
reports.role: The Education Committee scrutinises the work of the Department for Education, covering children’s social care, schools, colleges, the early years and higher education.

reports.title: Surviving drought: reclaim the rain
about: This inquiry focused on drought management practices and policies and consider whether these are sufficient for responding to current and future droughts. The inquiry will cover impacts, monitoring, engagement and changes in supply and demand, aiming to identify opportunities for improved drought preparedness and response in England.
reports.role: The Environment and Climate Change Committee was appointed to consider the environment and climate change.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how drought is managed in England, and whether current policies are enough for present and future droughts. It covered the effects of drought, monitoring, engagement and changes in water supply and demand, to find ways to be better prepared.

reports.title: Employment support for disabled people: Disability at Work
about: With the disability employment gap persistently at nearly 30%, the Government has announced it will spend an additional £2.2 billion on employment support over the next four years. reports.role: The Work and Pensions Committee looks into the policies and spending of the Department for Work and Pensions, including benefits for people in and out of work, state pensions and how private pensions are regulated.
reports.plain: The committee looked at why disabled people are less likely to be in work, a gap that has stayed at nearly 30%. The Government plans to spend an extra £2.2 billion on employment support over the next four years. This is the British Sign Language summary of the report.

Mandatory to manageable: the government’s plans for digital ID
reports.inquiry: Harnessing the potential of new digital forms of identification
about: Digital ID can refer to many different aspects of a person’s identity which can be recorded and stored digitally, including names and demographic information, digital versions of government-issued documents such as visas, or even biometric information like a fingerprint or face scan.
reports.role: The Home Affairs Committee is a cross-party committee of MPs responsible for scrutinising the work of the Home Office and its associated bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Government's plans for digital ID. Digital ID can cover many parts of a person's identity stored digitally, such as names, digital versions of documents like visas, or even a fingerprint or face scan.

reports.title: Health and Wellbeing
about: This inquiry will look into the health and wellbeing services available to those working in Parliament - exploring how existing services can be better communicated and supported, and identifying where some health and wellbeing needs are still not being met.
reports.role: The Administration Committee considers the services provided for Members, their staff and visitors by the House of Commons Service and makes recommendations to the House of Commons Commission, the Speaker and Officials on how those services are delivered.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the health and wellbeing services available to people who work in Parliament. It asked how existing services can be better explained and supported, and where some needs are still not being met.
