reports.title: Higher Education and Funding: Threat of Insolvency and International Students
about: The UK’s higher education sector is in trouble. Dozens of universities are making redundancies and cuts to courses, trying to stay afloat amid uncertainty over where their money is coming from.
reports.role: The Education Committee scrutinises the work of the Department for Education, covering children’s social care, schools, colleges, the early years and higher education.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the money problems facing universities and the role of international students. Dozens of universities are making redundancies and cutting courses to stay afloat, amid uncertainty over where their money will come from.

reports.title: Time is money: How regulators can support growth
about: The committee published its report Time is Money: How regulators can support growth on 12 May 2026, the Government response was published on 14 July 2026 and the report was debated 3 November 2026.
reports.role: The Industry and Regulators Committee was appointed to consider matters relating to industry, including the policies of His Majesty’s Government to promote industrial growth, skills and competitiveness, and to scrutinise the work of UK regulators.
reports.plain: The committee published its report on how regulators can support growth on 12 May 2026. The Government replied on 14 July 2026, and the report was debated on 3 November 2026.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: Failures at South East Water
about: UK water bodies are affected by a number of high-profile threats including agricultural and sewage pollution. The water sector faces other important concerns such as weak resilience of water supply systems and future water security.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the failures at South East Water, and at wider threats to UK water, including pollution from farming and sewage. It also looked at worries about whether water supplies can cope with problems and whether there will be enough water in future.

reports.title: The Bank of England’s Real-Time Gross Settlement Renewal Programme
about: The Bank of England (BoE) operates the Real-Time Gross Settlement system (RTGS) underpins UK payment systems including BACS and Visa. It enables high-value sterling payment transfers between financial institutions, processing around £750bn a day.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Bank of England's plan to renew the system that moves large payments between banks. The system, known as RTGS, underpins UK payment systems including BACS and Visa and processes around £750bn a day.

reports.title: AUKUS
about: This inquiry examined the AUKUS partnership, a trilateral security agreement between Australia, the US and the UK which was announced in 2021. AUKUS will see the US and UK support Australia in acquiring a nuclear-powered submarine fleet alongside a deepening of co-operation between the three countries on other advanced military technologies.
reports.role: The Defence Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration, and policy of the Ministry of Defence and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at AUKUS, a security agreement between Australia, the US and the UK announced in 2021. Under it, the US and UK will help Australia get a fleet of nuclear-powered submarines, and the three countries will work more closely on other advanced military technology.

reports.title: Fortifying the fiscal framework
about: The UK’s fiscal framework is intended to promote sustainable public finances. The framework includes a set of fiscal rules and institutional arrangements for monitoring the Government’s performance against those rules.
reports.role: The Economic Affairs Committee is a House of Lords permanent investigative committee charged with considering economic affairs.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the UK's fiscal framework, which is meant to keep public finances sustainable. It includes a set of fiscal rules and the arrangements for checking how the Government is performing against those rules.

reports.title: Scrutiny of International Agreements: Agreement between the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the European Union regarding Cooperation on the Application of their Respective Competition Laws
UK Aid and Development Assistance in a Fracturing World: Strengthening Resilience and Cooperation
reports.inquiry: Future of UK aid and development assistance
about: A new inquiry into the future of the UK’s international aid and development assistance programmes has been launched by the International Development Committee. It examined how the UK can continue to deliver high impact international aid and development assistance in the face of a 40% budget cut as the Government seeks to fund increased defence spending in the name of national security.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the UK can keep delivering high-impact international aid in the face of a 40% budget cut, as the Government seeks to pay for higher defence spending in the name of national security.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: Resetting the relationship with fishing communities
about: As it strives to deliver its energy, environmental and growth commitments, balancing the pressures on the marine environment will be a challenge for the Government. Following the UK’s exit from the EU, the UK takes part in several different international fisheries negotiations as an independent coastal state to agree total allowable catches (TACs) and quotas for fish stocks shared with other coastal states.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the Government deals with fishing communities. After leaving the EU, the UK negotiates as an independent coastal state to agree fishing limits and quotas for fish stocks it shares with other countries, while balancing pressures on the marine environment.

reports.title: Accountability in small government bodies
about: To ensure public money is spent and managed well, both Government departments and arms-length bodies must comply with a wide range of standards and requirements. This includes annual reporting and compliance with governance, planning and delivery expectations.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how accountable small government bodies are. To make sure public money is spent and managed well, departments and arms-length bodies must meet many standards, including annual reporting and rules on governance, planning and delivery.

reports.title: Addressing the risks from Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)
about: Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) are a large, complex group of about 14,000 synthetic chemicals used in a wide variety of everyday products. For example, PFAS are used to keep food from sticking to packaging or cookware, make clothes and carpets resistant to stains, and create firefighting foam that is more effective.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the risks from PFAS, a large group of about 14,000 man-made chemicals used in everyday products. They keep food from sticking to packaging or cookware, make clothes and carpets resist stains, and make firefighting foam more effective.

reports.committee: Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee
reports.title: Housing Conditions in Temporary Accommodation
about: The committee looked into the condition of homes in England.
reports.role: The Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee scrutinises the policy, administration and spending of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the condition of homes in England, focusing on temporary accommodation.

reports.title: Adjusting to new realities: rebalancing the UK-US partnership
reports.inquiry: The UK’s future relationship with the US
about: The committee looked into the future of UK-US relations.
reports.role: The International Relations and Defence Committee is appointed to consider the United Kingdom’s international relations and defence policy
reports.plain: The committee looked at the future of relations between the UK and the US.

reports.title: New Hospital Programme update
about: The New Hospital Programme (NHP) was announced in 2020, with a commitment to build 40 new hospitals to add to the deteriorating hospital estate by 2030. In January 2025, government confirmed that all schemes previously included in the programme would be delivered, including replacing seven hospitals constructed with deteriorating reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete, or RAAC.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the New Hospital Programme, announced in 2020 with a commitment to build 40 new hospitals by 2030. In January 2025 the Government confirmed that all schemes would go ahead, including replacing seven hospitals built with a weak type of concrete known as RAAC.

reports.committee: Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee
reports.title: Game On: Community and school sport
about: The Culture, Media and Sport Committee examined the health of sport in local communities and schools and whether more can be done to sustain and grow sporting opportunities for all. The inquiry looked at the funding available for sport in the community, how volunteers can be better supported and how to open up grassroots sport to under-represented groups.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the health of sport in local communities and schools and whether more can be done to grow sporting opportunities for everyone. It looked at funding, how volunteers can be better supported and how to open up grassroots sport to under-represented groups.

reports.committee: Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee
reports.title: Fan-led review of live and electronic music
about: The fan-led review of live and electronic music was launched by the House of Commons Culture, Media and Sport Committee in June 2025 and was independently chaired by Lord Brennan of Canton. The review brought music lovers together to discuss ideas to protect the industry and ensure it works in the best interests of fans.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee.
reports.plain: The committee ran a fan-led review of live and electronic music, launched in June 2025 and independently chaired by Lord Brennan of Canton. It brought music lovers together to discuss ideas to protect the industry and make sure it works in the best interests of fans.

reports.title: Combatting new forms of extremism
about: This inquiry examined the drivers of extremism in the UK, with a focus on emerging trends of young people being drawn into extremism, violence and crime through online radicalisation. It assessed whether the Government’s approach is keeping pace with the evolving threat and evaluate the effectiveness of measures such as Prevent in combatting new forms of extremism.
reports.role: The Home Affairs Committee is a cross-party committee of MPs responsible for scrutinising the work of the Home Office and its associated bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at what drives extremism in the UK, especially young people being drawn into extremism, violence and crime through online radicalisation. It asked whether the Government's approach is keeping pace and how effective measures such as Prevent are.

reports.title: The Future of HMP Parc
reports.inquiry: Prisons, Probation and Rehabilitation in Wales
about: Criminal justice in Wales exists within a unique policy environment, with prisons, probation and rehabilitation reserved to the UK Government, and key intersecting services like health, education and housing devolved to the Welsh Government. Wales is also unique in that, despite having five adult male prison facilities and a young offender institution, it has no prison for adult women.
reports.role: The Welsh Affairs Committee is responsible for scrutinising the expenditure, administration and policies of the Wales Office, and the policies of the UK Government as a whole that have an impact in Wales.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the future of HMP Parc. In Wales, prisons, probation and rehabilitation are the responsibility of the UK Government, while health, education and housing are devolved. Wales has five adult male prisons and a young offender institution but no prison for adult women.

reports.title: Pre-Appointment Hearing: Armed Forces Commissioner
reports.inquiry: Pre-appointment hearing for the Armed Forces Commissioner
reports.role: The Defence Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration, and policy of the Ministry of Defence and its associated public bodies.

reports.title: Historical Forced Adoption
about: In July 2022, the Joint Committee on Human Rights (the JCHR) published its report The Violation of Family Life: Adoption of Children of Unmarried Women 1949–1976 which examined the adoption practices in England and Wales during that time.
reports.role: The Education Committee scrutinises the work of the Department for Education, covering children’s social care, schools, colleges, the early years and higher education.
reports.plain: The committee looked at historical forced adoption. In July 2022 the Joint Committee on Human Rights published a report on the adoption of children of unmarried women between 1949 and 1976, which examined adoption practices in England and Wales at that time.

reports.title: Disinformation diplomacy: How malign actors are seeking to undermine democracy
about: Misinformation and disinformation campaigns are increasingly weaponised by hostile state and non-state actors and this inquiry sought to understand which actors are primarily responsible, and which channels and technologies are being used. It sought to map motivations, sources and locations of the most pressing disinformation threats to democracy, and to understand the impact of artificial intelligence.
reports.role: The Foreign Affairs Committee examines the expenditure, administration and policy of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and other bodies associated with the Foreign Office and within the Committee's remit, including the British Council.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how hostile states and other groups use disinformation to undermine democracy. It tried to find out who is mainly responsible and which channels and technologies they use, to map their motives and locations, and to understand the impact of artificial intelligence.

reports.title: The National Security Strategy
about: The Government published a new National Security Strategy (NSS) on 24 June 2025. The NSS reviews the risks facing the UK and sets out plans to address them, structured under three themes: security at home, strength abroad, and sovereign and asymmetric capabilities.
reports.role: The Joint Committee on the National Security Strategy scrutinises the structures for Government decision-making on national security, particularly the role of the National Security Council and the National Security Adviser.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the National Security Strategy, which the Government published on 24 June 2025. It reviews the risks facing the UK and sets out plans to deal with them under three themes: security at home, strength abroad, and sovereign and asymmetric capabilities.

reports.title: Government use of data analytics on error and fraud
about: Government lost between £55bn-£81bn to fraud and error in 2023-24. There are central platforms for public bodies to use to detect error and fraud, and in the same year these generated around £400m of savings.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the Government uses data analytics to catch error and fraud. The Government lost between £55bn and £81bn to fraud and error in 2023-24. Central platforms used to detect them generated around £400m of savings in the same year.

reports.title: New Towns: Creating Communities
reports.role: The Built Environment Committee was appointed to consider matters relating to the built environment, including policies relating to housing, planning, transport and infrastructure.

reports.title: Environmental regulation
about: Regulation is one of the main tools the government is using to make a success of the Environmental Improvement Plan. Government’s stated intention is to streamline regulation, to both safeguard nature and drive economic growth.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at environmental regulation. Regulation is one of the main tools the Government is using for its Environmental Improvement Plan, and it says it intends to streamline regulation to protect nature and drive economic growth.

reports.title: Palliative Care
about: The Health and Social Care Committee has established and commissioned a politically impartial panel of experts to conduct an evaluation – independently of the Committee – of palliative care in England. The Expert Panel will produce a report after each evaluation which will be sent to the Committee to review.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee set up a panel of experts, politically impartial and independent of the committee, to evaluate palliative care in England. The panel produces a report after each evaluation, which is sent to the committee to review.

reports.title: Peace under pressure: Protecting Women, Peace and Security
about: The committee looked into how the UK Government is involving the needs and voices of women in its development efforts. The cross-party committee of MPs explored the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda, adopted by the United Nations, and considered how this agenda is being incorporated into UK aid programmes, amid plans for the UK’s aid budget to be cut to 0.3% of GNI by 2027.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the UK Government is including the needs and voices of women in its development work. It explored the Women, Peace and Security agenda adopted by the United Nations and how it is built into UK aid, as the aid budget is planned to be cut to 0.3% of national income by 2027.

reports.title: Large Print - 10th Report - Peace under pressure: Protecting Women, Peace and Security
about: The committee looked into how the UK Government is involving the needs and voices of women in its development efforts. The cross-party committee of MPs explored the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda, adopted by the United Nations, and considered how this agenda is being incorporated into UK aid programmes, amid plans for the UK’s aid budget to be cut to 0.3% of GNI by 2027.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the UK Government is including the needs and voices of women in its development work. It explored the Women, Peace and Security agenda adopted by the United Nations. This is the large print version of the report.

reports.title: Economic growth in Northern Ireland: new and emerging sectors
about: Kickstarting economic growth is the number one mission for this Government’s term in office. In this inquiry, the committee examined plans to deliver economic growth in Northern Ireland, including the recent UK Industrial Strategy, with a particular reference to emerging sectors or ‘industries of the future’.
reports.role: The Committee examines the expenditure, administration and policy of the Northern Ireland Office and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at plans to grow Northern Ireland's economy, including the UK Industrial Strategy. It paid particular attention to new and emerging sectors, which are described as the industries of the future.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: Erosion of trust: the impact of coastal erosion on communities
about: The UK is facing increasingly frequent and severe environmental and weather-related events, including storms, flooding, heatwaves and wildfires. These, and other weather and climate related events, pose growing risks to public health, infrastructure, food production, and the natural environment.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the effects of coastal erosion on communities. The UK is facing more frequent and severe storms, floods, heatwaves and wildfires, which put public health, infrastructure, food production and nature at growing risk.

reports.title: Financial sustainability of adult hospices in England
about: In 2023, total UK hospice income of £1.8bn comprised around £0.5bn of state funding and the remainder from charitable sources. In 2023-24, many adult hospices reported financial pressures and the threat of needing to cut services by up to 20% unless additional funding was given.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the finances of adult hospices in England. In 2023 total UK hospice income was £1.8bn, with around £0.5bn from the state and the rest from charity. In 2023-24 many hospices said they might have to cut services by up to 20% without extra funding.

reports.title: Post Office Horizon scandal: Justice for sub-postmasters
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.

reports.title: Earned Settlement: Examining the Government’s proposed reforms
about: The Government has announced major changes to eligibility for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), also known as settlement, and is planning to consult on the proposed changes later this year. The purpose of this inquiry is to evaluate the evidence for, and potential impact of, the planned changes to inform and feed into the new policy as it is being developed.
reports.role: The Home Affairs Committee is a cross-party committee of MPs responsible for scrutinising the work of the Home Office and its associated bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Government's planned changes to who can get Indefinite Leave to Remain, also known as settlement. It asked for the evidence on the changes and their likely impact, to feed into the new policy as it is developed.

reports.title: BBC World Service
about: Globally, the BBC World Service, which aims to reflect the UK, its culture and values to the world, had a weekly audience of 320m in 2023-24. Since 2022, the BBC has reduced expenditure on the BBC World Service, in part driven by falling licence fee income, with savings plans announced of £28.5m across its international services.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the BBC World Service, which had a weekly audience of 320m in 2023-24. Since 2022 the BBC has cut spending on it, partly because of falling licence fee income, with savings plans of £28.5m announced across its international services.

reports.title: Flying Blind: Innovation, Growth and the Regions
about: The committee looked into “Innovation, growth and the regions” to assess the role of the UK’s innovation ecosystem in achieving the Government’s mission to kickstart economic growth across the country.
reports.role: The Science and Technology Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of the Government Office for Science and associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the role of the UK's innovation system in helping to grow the economy across the whole country. This is part of the Government's mission to kickstart economic growth.

reports.title: Government’s use of external consultants
about: The current government’s intention is to halve spending on consultants, with a commitment to producing a strategic workforce plan for the civil service in 2025 that can properly balance the use of civil servants and external resources.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the Government uses external consultants. It intends to halve spending on them and has committed to producing a strategic workforce plan for the civil service in 2025 to balance the use of civil servants and outside help.

reports.title: AI, copyright and the creative industries
about: This inquiry explored the practical steps that would enable creative rightsholders to reserve and enforce their rights meaningfully in relation to AI systems; what levels of transparency and accountability can reasonably be expected from AI developers; and how licensing, attribution and labelling tools might support a viable marketplace for creative content.
reports.role: The Communications and Digital Committee considers the media, digital and the creative industries
reports.plain: The committee looked at AI, copyright and the creative industries. It explored the practical steps that would let creators reserve and enforce their rights against AI systems, how open AI developers should be, and how licensing, credit and labelling tools could support a fair market for creative work.

reports.title: Home-to-school transport
about: Many children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) must travel long distances to schools that can meet their needs.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at transport for children to school. Many children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities must travel long distances to schools that can meet their needs.

The Seventh Carbon Budget

reports.plain: The committee looked at the advice on the Seventh Carbon Budget from the Climate Change Committee. reports.plain: The committee looked at the Government's proposed reset of the UK's relationship with the European Union.

reports.title: Whole of Government Accounts 2023-24
about: The Whole of Government Accounts (WGA) consolidates the accounts of over 10,000 public organisations, including central government departments, local authorities, devolved administrations, the NHS and public corporations, to provide the most complete and accurate picture of the UK’s public finances. For the first time ever in 2022-23, the National Audit Office was unable to sign the WGA.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Whole of Government Accounts, which bring together the accounts of over 10,000 public organisations, including departments, councils, the NHS and devolved administrations, to give the most complete picture of the UK's public finances. In 2022-23 the National Audit Office was unable to sign them for the first time ever.

reports.title: Menstrual health of girls and young women
reports.inquiry: Reproductive health conditions: girls and young women
about: The Committee is following up its previous work on women’s reproductive health, with a focus on better meeting the needs of girls and young women. It is assessing progress in diagnoses, treatments and pain management of conditions including endometriosis, adenomyosis and heavy menstrual bleeding.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee followed up its earlier work on women's reproductive health, focusing on the needs of girls and young women. It assessed progress on diagnosis, treatment and pain management for conditions including endometriosis, adenomyosis and heavy menstrual bleeding.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: Pre-appointment hearing with the Government's preferred candidate for the Chair of the Competition and Markets Authority
reports.inquiry: Appointment of Doug Gurr as Chair of the Competition and Markets Authority
about: On Tuesday 24 February the House of Commons Business and Trade Committee will question former head of Amazon UK Doug Gurr to assess his suitability for the role of Chair of the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), prior to the Secretary of State confirming him in post. After the hearing the Committee will prepare its report on the appointment, which will be published as soon as possible afterwards.

The session explored the intelligence that informed the decision, the options considered by West Midlands Police, and the political context.

reports.title: Rebuilding forensic science for criminal justice: an urgent need
about: The House of Lords Science and Technology Committee is conducting a short inquiry into forensic science, following up on its 2019 inquiry and the recent work from the Westminster Commission on Forensic Science, which described the sector as being in a ‘graveyard spiral’.
reports.role: The Science and Technology Committee is appointed to consider science and technology.
reports.plain: The House of Lords committee carried out a short inquiry into forensic science, following up on its 2019 inquiry and on recent work from the Westminster Commission on Forensic Science, which described the sector as being in a graveyard spiral.

reports.title: NS&I’s transformation programme
about: National Savings and Investments (NS&I), which borrows on behalf of government from retail investors via products such as premium bonds, has around 25m savers with over £230bn invested. It is undertaking a business transformation programme to replace Atos as the single supplier of its back-office and customer-facing functions with a multi-supplier model.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the transformation of National Savings and Investments, which borrows for the Government from savers through products such as premium bonds. It has around 25m savers with over £230bn invested, and is replacing Atos as its single supplier with several suppliers.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: Small business strategy
about: At the Autumn Budget 2024, the government announced its intention to publish a Small Business Strategy “setting out the government’s vision for support for small businesses”. This will be published in 2025.
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Government's plans for a Small Business Strategy. At the Autumn Budget 2024 the Government said it would publish a strategy setting out its vision for supporting small businesses, due in 2025.

reports.title: Foundations of Learning: replacing RAAC and securing school buildings
reports.inquiry: Reinforced Autoclaved Aerated Concrete (RAAC) and management of school estates
about: This one off session follows up the RAAC crisis in schools in the summer of 2023 and the work that followed by DfE and schools to remediate faulty end-of-life concrete in school buildings. It will also look into school estate management more broadly to consider other problems within the built environment of schools and what steps are needed to address these.
reports.role: The Education Committee scrutinises the work of the Department for Education, covering children’s social care, schools, colleges, the early years and higher education.
reports.plain: The committee held a one-off session on replacing RAAC in schools. It followed up on the RAAC crisis in the summer of 2023 and the work by the Department for Education and schools to deal with faulty, worn-out concrete, and looked more widely at how school buildings are managed.

reports.title: Tackling fraud and error in benefit expenditure 2024-25
about: In 2023-24, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) spent £268.5bn on benefit and pension payments. That same year, the National Audit Office (NAO) reported that benefit overpayments by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) were at £9.7bn, their highest ever level in cash terms, with the majority of overpayments accounted for by Universal Credit.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at fraud and error in benefit spending. In 2023-24 the Department for Work and Pensions spent £268.5bn on benefits and pensions, and the National Audit Office reported overpayments of £9.7bn, the highest ever in cash terms, mostly in Universal Credit.

reports.title: Rail investment pipelines: ending boom and bust
about: The Transport Committee examined investment pipelines for the railway.
reports.role: The Transport Committee is nominated by the House of Commons to scrutinise the Department for Transport.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how investment in the railway is planned, known as investment pipelines.

reports.title: Railways Bill
about: The Government has introduced the Railways Bill to Parliament to legislate for its commitment to unify network operations with infrastructure management under a single organisation – Great British Railways. The Bill is expected to go through ‘line by line’ scrutiny by a Public Bill Committee, which is separate to the Transport Committee.
reports.role: The Transport Committee is nominated by the House of Commons to scrutinise the Department for Transport.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Railways Bill, which the Government introduced to bring running the rail network and looking after its infrastructure under a single organisation, Great British Railways. A separate Public Bill Committee goes through the Bill line by line.

reports.committee: Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee
reports.title: Housing Conditions in the Social Rented Sector
about: The committee looked into the condition of homes in England.
reports.role: The Housing, Communities and Local Government Committee scrutinises the policy, administration and spending of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the condition of homes in England, focusing on the social rented sector.

reports.title: Operation Kenova: naming Stakeknife
about: This session considered the final report of Operation Kenova published on 9 December 2025 and follows up on our predecessor committee's consideration of the interim report published on 8 March 2024.
reports.role: The Committee examines the expenditure, administration and policy of the Northern Ireland Office and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee held a session on the final report of Operation Kenova, published on 9 December 2025. It followed up on the earlier committee's look at the interim report, published on 8 March 2024.

reports.title: Sifting of proposed negative Statutory instruments
reports.role: The Transport Committee is nominated by the House of Commons to scrutinise the Department for Transport.

reports.committee: Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee
reports.title: UK-EU agritrade: making an SPS agreement work
about: Animal and plant diseases and pests have far-reaching impacts on the environment, agricultural and horticultural sectors, trade, human health, animal welfare, and the food that we eat.
reports.role: The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee (EFRA) scrutinises the work of the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).
reports.plain: The committee looked at the UK-EU agreement on food and farming standards, known as an SPS agreement. Animal and plant diseases and pests have wide effects on the environment, farming, trade, human health, animal welfare and the food we eat.

reports.title: Future of UK aid and development assistance: interim report
reports.inquiry: Future of UK aid and development assistance
about: A new inquiry into the future of the UK’s international aid and development assistance programmes has been launched by the International Development Committee. It examined how the UK can continue to deliver high impact international aid and development assistance in the face of a 40% budget cut as the Government seeks to fund increased defence spending in the name of national security.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the UK can keep delivering high-impact international aid in the face of a 40% budget cut, as the Government seeks to pay for higher defence spending in the name of national security. This was an interim report.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: Toward a new doctrine for economic security: Government Response
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.

reports.title: Efficiency and resilience of the Probation Service
about: Reforms of probation services were carried out in 2014, which divided the service into two – a National Probation Service, dealing with the most serious offenders, and twenty-one private sector-led Community Rehabilitation Companies, dealing with lower-risk offenders. These reforms were heavily criticised, and the service was reunified in 2021 with the aim of delivering a more sustainable system.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how efficient and resilient the Probation Service is. Reforms in 2014 split it in two, and were heavily criticised, so it was brought back together in 2021 to build a more sustainable system.

reports.title: Medicines security-a national priority
about: Medicine shortages across England are increasing, which in turn impacts the health of patients, and puts significant pressure on the NHS, Pharmacies and GPs. The aim of this inquiry is to understand the causes of medicine shortages, and understand the UK's capabilities in predicting and preventing medicine supply issues, and minimising patient harms.
reports.role: The Public Services Committee was appointed to consider public services, including health and education.
reports.plain: The committee looked at why medicine shortages are growing across England, which affect patients' health and put pressure on the NHS, pharmacies and GPs. It also looked at how well the UK can predict and prevent supply problems and limit harm to patients.

reports.title: Scrutiny of international agreements: UK-India Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
about: Following the announcement of the UK-India Free Trade Agreement, the International Agreements Committee is opening an inquiry investigating the impacts and implications of the FTA for the UK. Our inquiry investigated the terms of the FTA, any potential benefits and disadvantages to the UK, and examine how key provisions will work for important sectors.
reports.role: The Committee scrutinises all treaties subject to ratification that are laid before Parliament under the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010 and considers other issues relating to the negotiation, conclusion and implementation of international agreements.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the UK-India trade agreement after it was announced. It investigated the terms of the deal, its possible benefits and disadvantages for the UK, and how its key provisions will work for important sectors.

reports.title: Costs of clinical negligence
about: The PAC in its 2025 scrutiny the Department of Health and Social Care’s (DHSC) annual report and accounts 2023-24 called on government to reduce tragic incidences of patient harm. The PAC found it unacceptable that DHSC had yet to develop a plan to deal with the cost of clinical negligence claims, with so much taxpayers’ money being spent on legal fees.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the cost of clinical negligence claims. In 2025 it found it unacceptable that the Department of Health and Social Care had no plan to deal with these costs, with so much taxpayers' money going on legal fees.

reports.title: Discrimination, harassment and abuse against Muslim women
about: This is a one off session examining issues around gendered Islamophobia. The session aims to understand the specific challenges facing Muslim women in the UK today.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee held a one-off session on gendered Islamophobia. It aimed to understand the particular challenges facing Muslim women in the UK today.

reports.title: Large Print - 10th Report - Discrimination, harassment and abuse against Muslim women
about: This is a one off session examining issues around gendered Islamophobia. The session aims to understand the specific challenges facing Muslim women in the UK today.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee held a one-off session on gendered Islamophobia. It aimed to understand the particular challenges facing Muslim women in the UK today. This is the large print version of the report.

reports.title: Increasing police productivity
about: Total police funding in 2025-26 is £19.6bn, with approx. 70% of this made up of central government funding and the rest raised through council tax. Government is aiming to put 13,000 additional police officers, police community support officers and special constables into neighbourhood policing roles, paid for by tackling waste through a programme of reform.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how to make policing more productive. Police funding in 2025-26 is £19.6bn, about 70% from central government and the rest from council tax. The Government aims to put 13,000 more officers and staff into neighbourhood policing.

reports.title: Engine for growth: securing skills for transport manufacturing
about: The UK has a long tradition of manufacturing motor vehicles, buses, aeroplanes, trains, and ships, but manufacturers in the transport industries are concerned about skills shortages. This inquiry explored current and future skills needs across the transport manufacturing sectors, and how the Government can support transport manufacturing in the UK by planning and investing in skills.
reports.role: The Transport Committee is nominated by the House of Commons to scrutinise the Department for Transport.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the skills needed for transport manufacturing, such as cars, buses, aeroplanes, trains and ships. Manufacturers are worried about skills shortages, so the committee asked what skills are needed now and later, and how the Government can help.

reports.title: Faulty energy efficiency installations
about: The Energy Company Obligation 4 (ECO4) and the Great British Insulation Scheme (GBIS), both funded via energy consumers’ bills, are government schemes for the installation of energy-efficiency improvements in people’s homes, such as insulation.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at faulty energy efficiency work in people's homes. Two government schemes, ECO4 and the Great British Insulation Scheme, are paid for through energy bills and fit improvements such as insulation.

reports.title: Draft Scotland Act 1998 (Modification of Schedule 5) Order 2026
reports.role: The Scottish Affairs Committee scrutinises the expenditure, administration and policies of the Scotland Office, and its associated bodies.

reports.title: First 1000 days: a renewed focus
reports.inquiry: The First 1000 Days: a renewed focus
about: The first 1000 days of life, from conception to age two, are widely recognised as a critical period for child development, shaping long-term health, well-being, and life outcomes.The previous Committee examined this period in its 2019 First 1000 days of life inquiry considering national strategy, current spending and barriers to investment and local provision.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the first 1000 days of life, from conception to age two, which are widely seen as a critical period for child development. The previous committee looked at this in 2019, considering national strategy, spending and barriers to investment and local services.

reports.committee: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee
reports.title: UK-India Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
reports.inquiry: UK trade with the US, India and EU
about: The committee looked into the UK’s trade deals with three of its most important partners: the United States, India, and the European Union. As part of this work, the Committee will scrutinise the detail and implementation of three recent developments: the India Free Trade Agreement; the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal; and the outcomes agreed following the recent UK-EU Summit.
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the UK's trade deals with its three most important partners: the United States, India and the European Union. It looked closely at the detail and rollout of the India trade deal, the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal and what was agreed at the UK-EU Summit.

reports.title: Artificial intelligence in financial services
about: The committee looked into how the UK financial services can take advantage of the opportunities in AI while mitigating any threats to financial stability and safeguarding financial consumers, particularly vulnerable consumers.
reports.role: The Treasury Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration and policy of HM Treasury, HM Revenue & Customs, and associated public bodies, including the Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how UK financial services can take advantage of AI while limiting threats to financial stability. It also looked at how to protect financial customers, particularly vulnerable ones.

reports.title: Financial sustainability of children’s care homes
about: The numbers of looked after children increased by 19% to 83,360 between 2015-16 and 2023-24. Around 16% of looked after children are accommodated in children’s homes.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the finances of children's care homes. The number of looked after children rose by 19% to 83,360 between 2015-16 and 2023-24, and around 16% of them live in children's homes.

reports.title: The appointment of Emma Douglas as Chair of the Pensions Regulator
reports.inquiry: Pre-appointment hearing: Chair of the Pensions Regulator
reports.role: The Work and Pensions Committee looks into the policies and spending of the Department for Work and Pensions, including benefits for people in and out of work, state pensions and how private pensions are regulated.

reports.title: Pension Schemes Bill
reports.role: The Constitution Committee examines all public bills for constitutional implications and investigates broad constitutional issues.

reports.title: Private markets: Unknown unknowns
reports.inquiry: Growth of private markets in the UK following reforms introduced after 2008
about: This inquiry looks into the growth of private markets in the UK following reforms introduced after 2008. In particular, the inquiry examined whether the regulatory capital and liquidity reforms introduced after 2008 have reduced banks’ ability or willingness to lend, pushing risk away from the banking sector and towards private markets.
reports.role: The Financial Services Regulation Committee was appointed to consider the regulation of financial services.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the growth of private markets in the UK after reforms brought in following 2008. It asked whether those reforms have made banks less able or willing to lend, pushing risk away from banks and towards private markets.

reports.title: DWP follow-up: Autumn 2025
about: The Public Accounts Committee will be following up recent scrutiny with the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) in autumn 2025, on various topics. The PAC’s July 2025 report on Jobcentres warned that government seemed complacent at the potential impact of a reduction in support for benefit claimants.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee followed up on its recent scrutiny of the Department for Work and Pensions in autumn 2025. Its report in July 2025 on Jobcentres warned that the Government seemed complacent about the effect of reduced support for people claiming benefits.

reports.title: Ministry of Justice follow-up: Autumn 2025
about: The Public Accounts Committee will be following up recent scrutiny with the Ministry of Justice in autumn 2025, on various topics. The PAC’s 2024 report into legal aid expressed deep concerns about MoJ’s and the Legal Aid Agency’s lack of curiosity on the impact of decreasing numbers of providers on people’s access to legal aid, despite evidence which suggests access is getting more difficult.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee followed up on its recent scrutiny of the Ministry of Justice in autumn 2025. Its 2024 report on legal aid expressed deep concern about a lack of curiosity over how fewer providers affects people's access to legal aid, though evidence suggests access is getting harder.

reports.title: Preparing for an ageing society
about: The UK is an ageing society. The birth rate is declining and life expectancy increasing; the UK can therefore expect an increasing proportion of its population to comprise older individuals.
reports.role: The Economic Affairs Committee is a House of Lords permanent investigative committee charged with considering economic affairs.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how the UK can prepare for an ageing society. The birth rate is falling and life expectancy is rising, so the UK can expect older people to make up a growing share of the population.

reports.title: Government services: Identifying costs
reports.inquiry: Government services: Identifying costs and generating income
about: The committee looked into government’s management of fees and charges to recover the costs of providing services and how government is identifying costs to sustainably improve productivity. Improved productivity is key to the government’s aims to improve the affordability of public services.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how government manages fees and charges to recover the cost of providing services, and how it identifies those costs to improve productivity. Better productivity is key to the Government's aim of making public services more affordable.

reports.title: The Building Safety Regulator: Building a better regulator
about: The report The Building Safety Regulator: Building a better regulator was published on 11 December 2025. The Government response was published on 11 February 2026.
reports.role: The Industry and Regulators Committee was appointed to consider matters relating to industry, including the policies of His Majesty’s Government to promote industrial growth, skills and competitiveness, and to scrutinise the work of UK regulators.
reports.plain: The committee published its report on the Building Safety Regulator on 11 December 2025. The Government replied on 11 February 2026.

reports.title: Access to the House of Commons and its Procedures
about: One of the most frequently raised areas of interests during the committee’s call for views has been accessibility. This inquiry considered the accessibility of the physical parliamentary estate and of Parliamentary procedures, language and information.
reports.role: The Modernisation Committee is a cross-party committee of MPs that considers reforms to House of Commons procedures, standards, and working practices.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how accessible the House of Commons is. Accessibility was one of the topics most often raised in its call for views, and the inquiry covered both the buildings and Parliament's procedures, language and information.

reports.title: Government services: Generating income
reports.inquiry: Government services: Identifying costs and generating income
about: The committee looked into government’s management of fees and charges to recover the costs of providing services and how government is identifying costs to sustainably improve productivity. Improved productivity is key to the government’s aims to improve the affordability of public services.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how government manages fees and charges to recover the cost of providing services, and how it identifies those costs to improve productivity. Better productivity is key to the Government's aim of making public services more affordable.

reports.role: The Joint Committee on Human Rights consists of twelve members, appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords, to examine matters relating to human rights within the United Kingdom, as well as scrutinising every Government Bill for its compatibility with human rights.

reports.committee: Energy Security and Net Zero Committee
reports.title: Workforce planning to deliver clean, secure energy
about: The committee looked into how to build the workforce that is needed to deliver the policies and infrastructure for the UK’s clean, secure energy mission.
reports.role: The Energy Security and Net Zero Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and its public bodies, including Ofgem and the Committee on Climate change.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how to build the workforce needed to deliver the policies and infrastructure for the UK's clean, secure energy mission.

reports.title: Espionage cases and the Official Secrets Acts
reports.role: The Joint Committee on the National Security Strategy scrutinises the structures for Government decision-making on national security, particularly the role of the National Security Council and the National Security Adviser.

reports.title: Community Mental Health Services
about: The committee looked into community mental health services. The inquiry examined what good looks like from the perspective of service users and their families/carers.
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Health and Social Care Committee.
reports.plain: The committee looked at community mental health services. It examined what good looks like from the point of view of the people who use the services and their families and carers.

reports.title: The Government's new approach to addressing the legacy of the past in Northern Ireland
about: The committee looked into Government policy on the legacy of the past in Northern Ireland. On 4 December 2024, the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland announced the Government’s next steps to ‘repeal and replace’ the Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy and Reconciliation) Act 2023.
reports.role: The Committee examines the expenditure, administration and policy of the Northern Ireland Office and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at Government policy on dealing with the legacy of the past in Northern Ireland. On 4 December 2024 the Secretary of State announced the next steps to repeal and replace the Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy and Reconciliation) Act 2023.

reports.committee: Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee
reports.title: Pre-appointment hearing for the Chair of the Charity Commission
reports.role: Welcome to the cross-party Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee.

reports.title: Toward a new doctrine for economic security
reports.role: The Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee scrutinises the policy, spending and administration of the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and its public bodies.

reports.title: Report - Time to deliver: The Autism Act 2009 and the new autism strategy
reports.role: The Autism Act 2009 Committee was appointed to consider the Autism Act 2009 and to make recommendations.

reports.title: BBC Accounts and Trust Statement 2024-25
about: An average 85% of UK adults use the BBC each week, spending 6hr26min watching BBC TV/iPlayer. In 2023-24, there were 23.9 million TV licences in force at the end of the year, around 775,000 of which were free licences for those aged over 75.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the BBC's accounts. On average 85% of UK adults use the BBC each week, spending 6hr26min watching BBC TV or iPlayer. In 2023-24 there were 23.9 million TV licences in force, around 775,000 of them free licences for people over 75.

reports.title: The rule of law: holding the line against tyranny and anarchy
about: The Committee published its report The rule of law: holding the line against tyranny and anarchy on 20 November 2025. The Government responded on 23 February 2026.
reports.role: The Constitution Committee examines all public bills for constitutional implications and investigates broad constitutional issues.
reports.plain: The committee published its report on the rule of law on 20 November 2025. The Government replied on 23 February 2026.

reports.title: The UK contribution to European Security
about: This inquiry examined the UK’s contribution to European Security. It examined the UK's contribution to NATO and its bilateral defence relationships with other European countries.
reports.role: The Defence Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to examine the expenditure, administration, and policy of the Ministry of Defence and its associated public bodies.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the UK's contribution to European security. That included its part in NATO and its defence relationships with individual European countries.

reports.title: Reducing NHS waiting times for elective care
about: The NHS’ statutory waiting standards for planned non-emergency, or elective, care are that 92% of patients should begin treatment within 18 weeks. Patients on 59% of pathways, or 4.4m people, were waiting less than 18 weeks at the end of 2024.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at how to cut NHS waiting times for planned, non-emergency care. The standard is that 92% of patients should start treatment within 18 weeks, but at the end of 2024 patients on 59% of pathways, or 4.4m people, were waiting less than 18 weeks.

reports.title: Tackling HIV transmission
reports.inquiry: The prevalence of sexually transmitted infections
about: This session explored trends in rates of STIs, including among particular groups, and the effectiveness of Government strategies aimed at reducing their prevalence. The session will also cover HIV and access to PrEP.
reports.role: The Women and Equalities Committee examines the work of the Office for Equality and Opportunity (OEO).
reports.plain: The committee held a session on rates of sexually transmitted infections, including among particular groups, and on how well the Government's strategies are working to reduce them. It also covered HIV and access to PrEP, a medicine that helps prevent HIV.

reports.title: Report - Social Mobility: Local Roots, Lasting Change
about: Read the key points in our report summary
reports.role: The Social Mobility Policy Committee was appointed to consider how educational and work opportunities could be better integrated to improve social mobility in the UK.

reports.title: Environmental sustainability and housing growth
Empowering Development: Energy Access for Communities
about: Energy lies at the core of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the 2015 Paris Agreement on Climate Change. Yet, the international community remains largely off track in meeting these commitments.
reports.role: The International Development Committee is appointed by the House of Commons to scrutinise the work of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office in respect of aid policy, and the expenditure of Official Development Assistance across UK government departments.
reports.plain: The committee looked at access to energy for communities in developing countries. Energy is at the core of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the 2015 Paris Agreement on Climate Change, yet the world is largely off track in meeting these commitments.

about: Energy lies at the core of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the 2015 Paris Agreement on Climate Change. Yet, the international community remains largely off track in meeting these commitments.

reports.plain: The committee looked at access to energy for communities in developing countries. Energy is at the core of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the 2015 Paris Agreement on Climate Change, yet the world is largely off track. This is the large print version of the report.

reports.title: Ending the cycle of reoffending - part one: rehabilitation in prisons
reports.inquiry: Rehabilitation and resettlement: ending the cycle of reoffending
about: The committee looked into Resettlement and Rehabilitation, which is centred around investigating the cycle of reoffending. HM Prison and Probation Service aims to reduce reoffending by rehabilitating the people in its care through education and employment.
reports.role: The Justice Committee examines the policies and spending of the Ministry of Justice (and associated public bodies).
reports.plain: The committee looked at resettlement and rehabilitation, investigating the cycle of reoffending. HM Prison and Probation Service aims to reduce reoffending by rehabilitating the people in its care through education and employment.

reports.title: Afghanistan Response Route
about: The Afghanistan Response Route (ARR) was set up by the Ministry of Defence to mitigate the security risks arising from a data protection breach and the unauthorised disclosure of personal information about Afghan citizens which occurred in February 2022. The National Audit Office (NAO) has published a report on the Afghanistan Response Route (ARR) to support the Committee’s scrutiny.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Afghanistan Response Route, set up by the Ministry of Defence to reduce the security risks after a data breach in February 2022 in which personal information about Afghan citizens was disclosed without permission. The National Audit Office published a report to support the committee's scrutiny.

reports.title: National Policy Statement for Ports
about: The committee looked into the Government’s proposal for a revised National Policy Statement for Ports (NPSP).
reports.role: The Transport Committee is nominated by the House of Commons to scrutinise the Department for Transport.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the Government's proposal for a revised National Policy Statement for Ports.

reports.title: Report - Is working from home working?
reports.role: The Home-based Working Committee was appointed to consider the effects and future development of home-based working in the UK.

reports.title: Unfinished Business: Resetting the UK-EU relationship
about: The committee looked into the reset of UK-EU relations that the Government is pursuing. The inquiry has two main themes: the substance of the reset, involving questions about what the reset is or should be; and the reset process, involving questions about how the Government pursues it with the EU and the role of interested parties in the UK.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the reset of UK-EU relations that the Government is pursuing. It had two main themes: what the reset is or should be, and how the Government goes about it with the EU, including the role of interested parties in the UK.

reports.title: Cost of maintaining the FCDO’s overseas estate
about: The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office’s (FCDO) overseas estate encompasses over 6,000 properties spread over almost 180 countries and valued at around £2.5 billion. The varied locations and uses of properties in this estate each present their own unique challenges which range from supply issues to security concerns.
reports.role: The Public Accounts Committee examines the value for money of Government projects, programmes and service delivery.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the cost of maintaining the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office's overseas estate. It covers over 6,000 properties in almost 180 countries, valued at around £2.5 billion, and each presents its own challenges, from supply issues to security concerns.

reports.title: Farming in Wales in 2025: Challenges and Opportunities
about: Wales has a long tradition of farming, and the sector is integral to the Welsh economy. In 2022, agriculture, fishing and forestry accounted for 1.8% of total employment in Wales and over 90% of the land area of Wales is utilised for farming.
reports.role: The Welsh Affairs Committee is responsible for scrutinising the expenditure, administration and policies of the Wales Office, and the policies of the UK Government as a whole that have an impact in Wales.
reports.plain: The committee looked at the challenges and opportunities for farming in Wales. In 2022 agriculture, fishing and forestry made up 1.8% of employment in Wales, and over 90% of the land area of Wales is used for farming.
